ex.en: The company held a luncheon for retiring staff.
ex.zh: 公司為退休員工舉辦了午宴。

ex.en: We are invited to a business luncheon on Monday.
ex.zh: 我們受邀參加星期一的商務午餐會。

ex.en: Let's meet at lunchtime.
ex.zh: 我們午餐時間見吧。

ex.en: The restaurant is always busy at lunchtime.
ex.zh: 這家餐廳午餐時間總是很忙。

ex.en: She left a lucrative job to start her own business.
ex.zh: 她辭去高薪工作，自己創業。

ex.en: The company won a lucrative contract.
ex.zh: 這家公司拿下了一份利潤豐厚的合約。

ex.en: That boy threw a lump of rock.
ex.zh: 那個男孩丟了一塊石頭。

ex.en: I bumped my head against the door and got a lump.
ex.zh: 我的頭撞到門，腫了一個包。

ex.en: Do you take one lump of sugar or two?
ex.zh: 你要加一顆方糖還是兩顆？

lump.zh: lump sum：一次付清的款項、一筆總額

ex.en: You can pay the fee in a lump sum.
ex.zh: 這筆費用可以一次付清。

ex.en: She received a lump sum when she retired.
ex.zh: 她退休時領了一筆一次性的退休金。

ex.en: The store lured customers with big discounts.
ex.zh: 這家店用大折扣吸引顧客。

ex.en: They tried to lure him to a rival company.
ex.zh: 他們想把他挖角到競爭對手的公司。

ex.en: The lure of a higher salary was hard to resist.
ex.zh: 更高薪水的誘惑讓人難以抗拒。

ex.en: Many young people come for the lure of city life.
ex.zh: 許多年輕人是被城市生活的吸引力而來的。

ex.en: Will you have time to have lunch with me?
ex.zh: 你有空跟我吃午餐嗎？

ex.en: If we begin early, we can finish by lunch.
ex.zh: 如果我們早點開始，就能在午餐前完成。

ex.en: The students' lunch period is from twelve to one.
ex.zh: 學生的午餐時間是十二點到一點。

ex.en: It was lucky for you that you found it.
ex.zh: 你能找到它真是幸運。

ex.en: This year has been a lucky one for him.
ex.zh: 今年對他來說是幸運的一年。

ex.en: Allan was lucky and passed the tax accountant examination.
ex.zh: 艾倫很幸運地考過了稅務師考試。

ex.en: Seven is my lucky number.
ex.zh: 七是我的幸運數字。

ex.en: He always wears his lucky shirt to interviews.
ex.zh: 他每次面試都穿他的幸運襯衫。

ex.en: Sooner or later, his luck will run out.
ex.zh: 他的好運遲早會用完。

ex.en: I don't believe that black cats cause bad luck.
ex.zh: 我不相信黑貓會帶來厄運。

ex.en: A little bit of luck sometimes leads to an unexpected success.
ex.zh: 一點點運氣有時會帶來意想不到的成功。

luck.zh: good luck / best of luck：祝好運、祝順利

ex.en: We wish you the best of luck in your endeavors.
ex.zh: 祝您一切順利。

ex.en: Good luck with your job interview!
ex.zh: 祝你面試順利！

ex.en: Advertisements urge us to buy luxuries.
ex.zh: 廣告慫恿我們買奢侈品。

ex.en: Travelling is a luxury I can't afford.
ex.zh: 旅行對我來說是負擔不起的奢侈。

ex.en: In the United States the automobile is a necessity and not a luxury.
ex.zh: 在美國，汽車是必需品而不是奢侈品。

ex.en: On the seventh floor, you can find four luxury restaurants.
ex.zh: 七樓有四間豪華餐廳。

ex.en: We stayed at a luxury hotel in Bangkok.
ex.zh: 我們在曼谷住了一間豪華飯店。

ex.en: He is afraid of getting lung cancer.
ex.zh: 他很怕得肺癌。

ex.en: Smokers are far more likely to develop lung cancer than non-smokers are.
ex.zh: 吸菸者罹患肺癌的機率遠高於不吸菸者。

ex.en: Regular exercise helps keep your lungs healthy.
ex.zh: 規律運動有助於維持肺部健康。

lung.zh: at the top of one's lungs：扯開嗓門、放聲

ex.en: He shouted at the top of his lungs.
ex.zh: 他扯開嗓門大喊。

ex.en: The kids sang at the top of their lungs.
ex.zh: 孩子們放聲高歌。

ex.en: We loaded a lot of luggage into the car.
ex.zh: 我們往車裡裝了很多行李。

ex.en: I don't like traveling with lots of luggage.
ex.zh: 我出門不喜歡帶很多行李。

ex.en: Let me help you with your luggage.
ex.zh: 讓我幫您提行李。
